items.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021
items.q: Every time I get on the bandstand with George Coleman I’m going to learn a new song.

ctx.x: I mean yes of course. That’s the biggest problem — probably one of the most fundamental problems with jazz education is an emphasis on reading music and not using your ear and not pulling the music away. But so much of this has to do with the

professional experience. You know there’s so fewer opportunities for younger players to work, to play, to perform on a regular basis, to apprentice with established players, to have to kind of sink or swim in that, on the bandstand so to speak. Those skills are just gone away. You know? If there were a lot more performing opportunities with a — that were still using the Great American Songbook you know, young sidemen would just have to buckle down and be able to learn and hear songs that they didn’t know on the…
Does it help because you had perfect pitch that you can listen to the bass player and that’s vital what the bass player is playing, especially if you don’t know a tune.
